Can you also check whether it shows up as two separate controllers on your PC?

@gwendolyn-personal Please use correct indentation in the code next time, it cannot be used like this. (Did you just write this here instead of copying it?) Adding `GDScript` after the first three backticks (`\``) also enables highlighting, making it more readable.

Here is the fixed script for reference:
(Renamed the unused parameter `connected` to `_connected` in `_on_joy_connection_changed`)

```GDScript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	Input.joy_connection_changed.connect(_on_joy_connection_changed)
	
	var controllers = Input.get_connected_joypads()
	for controller in controllers:
		var guid = Input.get_joy_guid(controller)
		var device_info = Input.get_joy_info(controller)
		var device_name = Input.get_joy_name(controller)
		
		print("Guid: ", guid, " Info: ", device_info, " name: ", device_name)

func _on_joy_connection_changed(device: int, _connected: bool) -> void:
	var guid = Input.get_joy_guid(device)
	var device_info = Input.get_joy_info(device)
	var device_name = Input.get_joy_name(device)
	
	print("Guid: ", guid, " Info: ", device_info, " name: ", device_name)

```

I will check this to confirm

I am running on linux, so I looked up some equivalents for joy.cpl, which is a windows tool. I used jstest-gpk to verify that there is only one controller connected, and also verified that there is only on js connection file in the input directory. Screenshots attached.

When this occurs for me, it causes devices[1] and devices[2] to be associated to the same physical device and so my code assigns the same controller to two players - does anyone know of a workaround for that problem?

> When this occurs for me, it causes devices[1] and devices[2] to be associated to the same physical device and so my code assigns the same controller to two players - does anyone know of a workaround for that problem?

Do you mean that `Input.get_connected_joypads()` returns `[1, 2]`?

You renamed the issue, does that mean that it's also reproducible with controllers other than the Xbox controllers?

It might be an SDL issue, but to confirm that a test app or a Godot version with `builtin_sdl` build flag set to `false` need to be prepared, unless Steam (that uses SDL) can also detect duplicate controllers.
